before: An investor prices a building from expected future rent. Which valuation principle underlies that decision?
DRE Appraisal identifies anticipation as the basis for converting future income benefits into present value.
after: An estate needs value as of last December, but inspection occurs in June. Which date governs the opinion?
The effective date identifies when the value opinion applies. Inspection and reporting may occur later; their dates do not replace the specified valuation date.
DRE15:The appraisal process and methods;effective date
rationales: Add effective-date application to appraisal process.

before: A modest house gains value from neighboring superior homes. Which appraisal principle describes this effect?
DRE Appraisal describes progression as enhanced value through association with similar properties of greater value. Regression is the opposite influence.
after: An appraisal request says only “value this building.” Which missing instruction defines how the result will be used?
Financing, sale, or another intended use
Narrative, form, or oral report format
Defining the appraisal problem includes identifying intended use. Choosing an approach, scheduling work and selecting a report format are separate decisions informed by that problem.
DRE15:The appraisal process and methods;intended use
rationales: Add assignment-purpose distinction without prescribing a method.

before: A comparable has +$40,000 and -$40,000 adjustments. What gross adjustment does its zero net conceal?
The absolute adjustments total $80,000 even though their net is zero. DRE Appraisal warns that large adjustments reduce comparability, so cancellation does not make a sale closely comparable.
after: A comparable was renovated after its sale. Which condition belongs in the comparison with the subject?
Condition when the appraiser inspected it
The comparison must reflect the property that actually sold. Using subsequent improvements would attribute features to a transaction that did not include them. Verify the condition at the sale date.
DRE15:Sales comparison procedure;condition at time of sale
rationales: Add data-verification step, replacing gross-adjustment arithmetic.

before: Which age estimate reflects maintenance and condition rather than elapsed years since construction?
DRE Appraisal uses effective age to reflect condition relative to a comparable building. It can differ substantially from chronological age.
after: Before collecting appraisal data, what decision determines the extent of inspection, research, and analysis needed?
After defining the problem, the appraiser determines the work needed to solve it. Data collection and analysis follow that decision; reconciliation follows the development of value indications.
DRE15:The appraisal process and methods;scope of work
rationales: Add distinct process sequencing and scope objective.

before: A rent roll omits recurring parking receipts. Which valuation input needs revision?
DRE Appraisal includes income from all sources, including parking, before deducting vacancy and operating expenses.
after: A lender engages an appraiser, but the buyer pays the appraisal fee. Who is the client for that assignment?
The appraisal client is the party engaging the appraiser for the assignment. Paying the fee or arranging access does not, by itself, establish the appraiser-client relationship.
rationales: Add property-interest problem definition, replacing redundant gross-income input.
Use directly verified client-identification process objective; distinguish engagement from payment.

before: What distinguishes appraisal depreciation from the owner's annual income-tax deduction?
Loss in value from any cause
DRE Appraisal expressly distinguishes market loss in value from book depreciation used for income-tax accounting.
after: Which federal body monitors state appraiser regulatory programs and reviews the Appraisal Foundation’s work?

The Appraisal Subcommittee oversees the regulatory framework for federally related transactions. It monitors state regulatory programs and the Appraisal Foundation; this is distinct from performing an individual property appraisal.
rationales: Add federal oversight objective.

before: Reconciliation weights a $450,000 sales indication 70% and a $500,000 income indication 30%. What value results?

The stipulated weights yield 0.70 times $450,000 plus 0.30 times $500,000, or $465,000. DRE Appraisal describes reconciliation as reasoned weighting, not automatically averaging differing approaches; these weights are supplied solely for this calculation.
after: An older warehouse has strong comparable sales but uncertain depreciation estimates. Which reconciliation gives that evidence appropriate influence?
More weight to the sales indication
More weight to the cost indication
Weight proportional to each indicated dollar value

Reconciliation considers the quality and reliability of the evidence supporting each approach. Strong comparable sales and uncertain depreciation support greater reliance on sales here, not equal or dollar-proportional weighting.
rationales: Replace stipulated weighted-average exercise with evaluation of conflicting evidence.

before: Which cost remains comparatively stable when occupancy falls from full capacity to seventy percent?
DRE Appraisal describes property taxes as fixed operating expenses with little direct correlation to occupancy. Other listed expenses depend more directly on use or turnover.
after: Which valuation is a real estate sales professional’s price estimate commonly used to support a listing price?

CFPB distinguishes a BPO prepared by a real estate sales professional from a computer-generated AVM and an appraisal by a licensed appraiser. A BPO commonly supports a listing price; it is not automatically interchangeable with a required appraisal.
rationales: Add BPO distinction.

before: Which instrument pledges the real property as collateral, distinct from the borrower’s promise to repay?
DRE Finance distinguishes the security instrument from the note evidencing the debt. This question does not assume a particular state’s title or foreclosure theory.
after: Under lien theory, how does granting a mortgage affect ownership before foreclosure?
Borrower retains title subject to security
Lender receives legal title as security
Borrower and lender become joint tenants
Lender receives the borrower’s equity outright

Lien theory treats the mortgage as an encumbrance while ownership remains with the borrower. Title theory instead treats legal title as security. State law controls which theory and foreclosure rules apply.
DRE5:Lien theory versus legal title theory
rationales: Replace note/security overlap with conditional theory comparison.

before: An FHA borrower finances an upfront insurance premium instead of paying cash. What financing consequence follows?
Higher loan balance and overall borrowing cost
Lower principal with an unchanged cash requirement
Replacement of the mortgage with a private policy
Elimination of the ongoing insurance charge
CFPB explains that financing the upfront FHA premium adds to the amount borrowed and overall cost; it does not remove the ongoing premium.
after: An applicant alters pay statements to show overtime never earned. Which mortgage-fraud element do those records supply?

False earnings records misstate income used in underwriting. OCC identifies deceit and incorrect application information as mortgage-fraud concerns. Occupancy, property condition and asset sourcing are different underwriting facts.
rationales: Replace self-cuing FHA cost item with concrete fraud classification.

before: Receipt of a Loan Estimate means which stage has occurred, without itself establishing final loan approval?
Underwriting has issued an unconditional commitment
Borrower has accepted every quoted closing charge
Seller has consented to the buyer’s financing
CFPB states that a Loan Estimate describes expected terms after application; it is not an approval or denial.
after: A lender sells completed mortgages to Freddie Mac and uses the proceeds for new loans. Which market function occurs?

Freddie Mac purchases qualifying loans from financial institutions in the secondary market. Sale proceeds let lenders make additional loans. Origination is the primary-market transaction with a borrower; a loan sale is not itself borrower refinancing.
rationales: Replace weak estimate item with secondary-market function.

before: For a covered mortgage, how early must the borrower receive the initial Closing Disclosure before closing?
CFPB describes the three-business-day review period for a covered mortgage. The rule does not apply identically to every credit product.
after: For a covered mortgage, how early must the borrower receive the initial Closing Disclosure before consummation?

The borrower must receive the initial Closing Disclosure at least three business days before consummation, when the borrower becomes contractually obligated on the credit transaction. Consummation is not necessarily the same event as funding or property transfer.
rationales: Use legal event rather than ambiguous closing.
Trace exact new regulatory sections.

before: Which fact distinguishes a bona fide settlement-service payment from a disguised referral fee under RESPA?
Payment corresponds to services actually performed
Payment is described as marketing in the invoice
Payment is issued after rather than before closing
Payment remains below an informal gift ceiling
CFPB explains that payment for actual goods or services may be permissible. Labels, timing and low value do not alone establish that it is not a referral fee.
after: A settlement provider pays $900 for work reasonably worth $300, with the excess rewarding referrals. What raises RESPA concerns?
Use of a written service agreement

Actual work does not shelter compensation for referrals. CFPB says service payments must reasonably relate to the value of the services; referral value is excluded. The stipulated excess rewards referrals even though some work occurred.
rationales: Include reasonable actual-service value and remove invoice safe harbor.

before: A covered settlement provider pays a broker solely for steering borrowers to it. What raises the RESPA Section 8 issue?
Value exchanged under a referral understanding
Payment for documented services actually performed
A lender’s discount directly to its own customer
A real estate brokerage’s permitted cooperative fee
CFPB explains that Section 8 prohibits things of value for settlement referrals involving federally related mortgage loans, while identifying specified exceptions.
after: A covered settlement provider pays a broker solely for steering borrowers to it. What raises the RESPA Section 8 issue?
Value exchanged under a referral understanding
Reasonable compensation solely for actual services
A lender’s discount directly to its own customer
A real estate brokerage’s permitted cooperative fee
CFPB explains that Section 8 prohibits things of value for settlement referrals involving federally related mortgage loans, while identifying specified exceptions.
rationales: Avoid suggesting any actual-service payment is exempt.

before: For how long must sellers and lessors retain signed federal lead-disclosure documentation after the sale or lease starts?
EPA specifies three years of retention from the sale date or the beginning of the leasing period.
after: Federal lead-disclosure records must be retained how long after a completed sale or the start of a lease?
EPA requires sellers and lessors to retain signed disclosure documentation for three years after the sale is completed or the leasing period begins.
rationales: Correct retention trigger.

before: How is a neighborhood improvement levy allocated differently from an ordinary ad valorem charge?
Original cost paid for affected parcels
Rental income earned from affected parcels
Mortgage debt secured by affected parcels

DRE Taxation explains benefit assessments as charges based on benefits received from an improvement. That allocation basis differs from an ordinary ad valorem charge based on assessed value; state procedures are not tested.
after: How is a special benefit assessment allocated differently from an ordinary ad valorem property tax?
Assessed market value of affected parcels
Original purchase cost of affected parcels
Outstanding mortgage balance on affected parcels

DRE Taxation explains benefit assessments as charges based on benefits received from an improvement. That allocation basis differs from an ordinary ad valorem charge based on assessed value; state procedures are not tested.
rationales: Identify benefit assessment expressly.

before: A city acquires land for a public road with compensation. Which power is being exercised?
DRE Transfer describes eminent domain as governmental acquisition for public use with compensation. It differs from the owner's voluntary dedication.
after: A city condemns land for a public road over the owner’s objection, with compensation. Which power applies?
DRE Transfer describes eminent domain as governmental acquisition for public use with compensation. It differs from the owner's voluntary dedication.
rationales: Make compulsory acquisition explicit.

before: A deed grants a park site subject to a use condition. How does this differ from an unrestricted fee?
Breach can expose ownership to forfeiture
Breach necessarily creates a mortgage lien
Breach converts the grantee into a tenant
DRE Property distinguishes a qualified or defeasible fee from fee simple absolute. A condition affecting continued ownership is different from a lien, lease or condition precedent.
after: A deed reserves a right of reentry for breach of a park-use condition. How does ownership differ from unrestricted fee?
Breach can expose ownership to forfeiture
Breach creates only a damages claim
Breach automatically renews a lease term

The express right of reentry makes the granted estate defeasible: a breach can expose ownership to forfeiture. A use covenant alone need not have that effect, and a right of reentry does not mean every breach automatically transfers title.
rationales: Distinguish defeasible ownership from a covenant.

before: A buyer receives a quitclaim from someone with no ownership interest. What has the buyer acquired through that deed?
Any estate the signer later acquires
Estate free of earlier recorded liens

DRE Principal Instruments states that a quitclaim conveys only an interest the grantor actually has, with no implied warranties or after-acquired title. Recording does not create ownership in the grantor.
after: A buyer receives a quitclaim from someone with no ownership interest. What has the buyer acquired through that deed?
Estate free of earlier recorded liens

A quitclaim transfers whatever interest the grantor has without guaranteeing ownership. Here the grantor has none, so no present estate passes. Any effect on later-acquired title depends on the instrument and governing law; it is not categorically excluded nationally.
rationales: Remove national after-acquired-title overstatement.

before: A deed-of-trust loan is repaid. Which instrument is used to return the trustee's interest?

DRE Principal Instruments describes reconveyance following satisfaction of the secured obligation. Assignment changes the beneficiary; subordination changes priority; extension changes the repayment schedule.
after: A deed-of-trust loan is repaid. Which instrument is used to return the trustee's interest?

Reconveyance returns the trustee’s interest following satisfaction of the secured obligation. Assignment changes the beneficiary, subordination changes priority, and modification changes existing loan terms rather than releasing the trustee’s interest.
rationales: Explain actual modification distractor.

before: A 60-by-100-foot floor contains a 20-by-30-foot open courtyard. What enclosed floor area remains?
Subtract the courtyard’s 600 square feet from the overall 6,000-square-foot rectangle. The dimensions describe an original area calculation within the outline’s math scope.
after: A 60-by-100-foot floor contains a 20-by-30-foot open courtyard. What enclosed floor area remains?
The overall rectangle is 60 × 100 = 6,000 square feet. The courtyard is 20 × 30 = 600 square feet. Subtracting the courtyard leaves 5,400 square feet enclosed.
rationales: Remove authoring commentary.

before: A $24,000 commission splits equally between firms; one agent receives 65% of that firm’s share. What does the agent receive?
The firm receives $12,000, of which 65% is $7,800. The percentages are contractual facts supplied for this original calculation.
after: A $24,000 commission splits equally between firms; one agent receives 65% of that firm’s share. What does the agent receive?
Each firm receives half of $24,000, or $12,000. The agent receives 65% of that share: $12,000 × 0.65 = $7,800.
rationales: Remove authoring commentary; ordinary sequential calculation is application.

before: Several brokerages publish similar fees. What additional fact most directly supports a price-fixing concern?
Evidence their office rents are similar
Evidence each firm reviewed public advertisements
FTC distinguishes a coordinated price agreement from parallel prices independently responding to market conditions.
after: Which part of a private apartment property is a public accommodation under ADA Title III?
Clubroom limited to residents and guests

DOJ distinguishes strictly residential areas from places serving the public within residential facilities. A public rental office is covered by Title III; private residential areas can be subject to other accessibility laws.
rationales: Replace repeated price-fixing distinction with ADA scope.

before: What can supply consideration in a bilateral sale agreement before any money changes hands?
DRE Transfer explains that a valid promise can be consideration for another promise. The exchange need not consist of an immediate cash payment.
after: A buyer may cancel at will without notice or obligation. What undermines that promise as consideration?
A commitment that leaves its maker free to withdraw at pleasure without obligation may be illusory. This differs from a genuine conditional promise or a small but real bargained-for exchange.
rationales: Replace reciprocal-promise overlap with illusory versus genuine conditional commitment.

before: A contract requires a loan commitment, not prequalification. Which document best supports removing that contingency?
DRE Transfer requires performance of the actual contractual condition. A preliminary affordability assessment does not establish the loan commitment expressly required here.
after: Purchase duties arise only after rezoning approval under the agreement. What function does approval serve?

A condition precedent must occur before the specified duty arises. It is distinct from a title promise, a predetermined breach remedy, or a transfer of contractual rights. The agreement expressly makes purchase duties conditional here.
rationales: Replace literal loan-commitment restatement with contractual-condition classification.

before: A contract expressly permits cancellation after a failed inspection. Why is timely exercise not necessarily breach?
It uses an agreed contractual right
It substitutes a new purchase contract
DRE Transfer recognizes discharge according to the parties' agreement. Exercising the stated cancellation right is different from failing to perform an unconditional obligation.
after: A contract expressly permits cancellation after a failed inspection. Why is timely exercise not necessarily breach?
Exercise of a contractual termination right
Avoidance for lack of contractual capacity
DRE Transfer recognizes discharge according to the parties' agreement. Exercising the stated cancellation right is different from failing to perform an unconditional obligation.
rationales: Use competing legal grounds instead of unrelated acts; downgrade label.

before: A valid contractual claim becomes time-barred. Which distinction explains why the original agreement was not necessarily void?
DRE Transfer distinguishes an unenforceable agreement from one void at formation. A limitations defense concerns enforcing the claim; no particular state's time period is tested.
after: A claim on a valid contract becomes barred by the applicable limitation period. Which classification describes the enforcement problem?

A limitation defense concerns enforcement of a claim. It does not establish that the original agreement lacked validity, resulted from fraud, or has been performed. No universal state limitation period is asserted.
rationales: Replace nonsense explanations with nearby contract classifications.

before: An agent alone claims unlimited signing power. What evidence is missing for apparent authority?
Agent's written assurance to the contractor
Agent's personal belief about signing powers
DRE Agency says the agent's acts alone do not establish apparent authority. Its foundation is an appearance attributable to the principal, with reasonable reliance by the third party.
after: Where consensual dual agency is permitted, whose informed consent must a broker obtain to represent buyer and seller?
Only the principal paying the commission
Only the principal accepting the offer

Dual agency creates duties to opposing principals, so informed consent concerns both represented parties. Payment and appointment order do not resolve that conflict. States differ on whether and how dual agency is permitted.
rationales: Replace second apparent-authority objective with dual-agency consent and explicit jurisdictional condition.

before: An owner authorizes emergency repairs and sets a routine spending cap. Which expenditure fits the separate emergency authority?
Stopping an active major water leak
DRE Agency discusses emergency authority to protect property where immediate action is necessary. The scenario expressly grants it separately from the routine spending limit.
after: Emergency authority permits stopping a burst pipe. Which work most closely fits that authority without broader renovation approval?
Isolate the leak and restore damaged pipe
Replace all building plumbing with upgraded fixtures
Reconfigure bathroom piping for a future remodel
Extend new water service to an unfinished addition
Emergency authority supports work necessary to address the immediate problem. It does not itself authorize an expanded renovation merely because the same contractor could perform it.
rationales: Compare repair scope within an emergency rather than emergency versus cosmetic work.

before: A broker delegates client work to an assistant. Which responsibility does the broker retain?
Assistant's duty to perform the task
Client's duty to pay agreed expenses
Principal's power to define the assignment
DRE Agency distinguishes delegating performance from shedding responsibility for the delegated duty. It emphasizes care when choosing a delegate and supervising performance.
after: A broker delegates document preparation, then fails to review repeated errors. Which retained duty is most directly implicated?

Delegating preparation does not remove responsibility for overseeing that work. The repeated unreviewed errors concern supervision; the other choices describe different duties without supporting facts here.
rationales: Distinguish dimensions of delegated agency responsibilities.

before: Two listings describe Lot 7, Block 2, but cite different recorded plats. What can the broker conclude?
Matching lot numbers identify one parcel
Equal assessed areas identify one parcel
DRE Property's lot-and-block method includes the referenced recorded map. Matching lot and block numbers in different plats do not identify one parcel.
after: “Lot 7, Block 2” appears on two subdivision plats. Which reference distinguishes the intended legal description?
Name and recording reference of the plat
Street address and present owner’s name
Assessor parcel number and assessment year
Seller’s deed date and purchase price
DRE Property's lot-and-block method includes the referenced recorded map. Matching lot and block numbers in different plats do not identify one parcel.
rationales: Use concrete map identification instead of uniquely cautious answer.
Use competing parcel-identification information instead of unrelated transaction dates.

before: A seller requests diversion of the buyer's repair credit. What would authorize the neutral escrow holder to change allocations?

DRE Escrow limits the holder to the principals' instructions. Changing an agreed buyer credit requires their authority, rather than a unilateral request or instructions governing a different relationship.
after: Buyer and seller jointly reduce a repair credit from $5,000 to $3,000. Seller later demands $1,000. Which instruction governs?

The joint amendment changes the affected principals’ instructions to $3,000. The seller’s later unilateral demand does not supply the buyer’s authority to reduce that credit again. The holder cannot invent a compromise.
rationales: Make competing authorizations concrete within escrow.

before: Two beneficiary ledgers show $8,000 and negative $300. Why does a $7,700 bank balance not resolve the problem?
Every positive ledger must equal the bank
Bank interest necessarily explains the deficit
Separate records identify each beneficiary’s funds. Agreement in the total does not establish that funds remain available for each beneficiary.
after: Accurate owner ledgers show A: $8,000 and B: −$300. What does the negative entry reveal despite a reconciled total?
B’s disbursements exceed B’s available funds by $300
A’s disbursements exceed A’s available funds by $300
B has $300 remaining for further disbursement
A’s positive balance is overstated by $300

The negative B balance indicates $300 more was disbursed for B than B had available. A matching $7,700 total does not provide each beneficiary’s required funds. Reconciliation does not erase the separate deficit.
rationales: Replace generalized safe answer with interpretation of accurate beneficiary entries.

before: An agent falsely reports no vacancies to one racial group. Why can equal published rents fail to cure discrimination?
False availability can deny housing access
Price equality controls over access differences
Protection begins only after a written application
Racial discrimination requires a higher rent charge
DOJ identifies false availability as a way of denying equal housing opportunity. An unequal price is not necessary.
after: An agent tells callers of one race that an available apartment has already been rented. Which prohibited act occurs?

The Fair Housing Act prohibits falsely denying that housing is available because of race. This conduct does not require unequal published rents; the facts concern availability statements, not financing or advertising.
rationales: Use competing prohibited practices, not equal-price justification strawmen.

before: Which permissions best fit a photographer assigned to prepare listing images under FTC’s least-privilege principle?
Property photos and approved access instructions
Property photos and seller financial statements
All listing files with read-only permissions
All office records during the photography appointment
FTC recommends access limited to resources needed for the job. Read-only or time-limited access can still expose unrelated sensitive records.
after: An auditor must inspect client ledgers but has no posting duties. Which permissions apply least privilege?
Read-only access to every client file

The auditor needs to read the relevant accounting records, not post transactions or access all client files. Read-only access can still be too broad; temporary access can still grant unnecessary powers.
rationales: Test minimum access with concrete permission tradeoffs.

before: Which vendor oversight measure tests whether a brokerage’s do-not-call policy actually reaches calling operations?
Compare dialed numbers against current suppression lists
Confirm the contract includes a compliance warranty
Verify that agents received the written policy
Review the vendor’s published compliance statement
FTC says sellers should monitor and enforce compliance. Comparing actual calling activity with suppression records tests implementation beyond promises or policy distribution.
after: Which comparison most directly tests whether a calling vendor honored a brokerage’s entity-specific opt-outs?
Call timestamps against effective suppression dates
Call volumes against agents’ assigned quotas
Answered calls against scheduled dialing windows
Consumer inquiries against vendor invoice totals

Comparing actual calls with the dates opt-outs became effective tests whether suppression reached operations. Volume, timing windows and billing comparisons examine other operational controls, not whether these consumers were suppressed.
rationales: Use competing operational audit comparisons rather than promises.

before: A landlord has lead reports covering common hallways in a covered apartment building. Which disclosure scope applies?
Only reports for the rented unit are included
Only reports ordered by this tenant are included
Common-area records wait until lease renewal
EPA states that available common-area information is included in applicable multiunit lead disclosures.
after: A landlord has lead reports covering common hallways in a covered apartment building. Which disclosure scope applies?
Available records confined to the leased unit
Available records confined to occupied units
Available records confined to exterior surfaces
EPA states that available common-area information is included in applicable multiunit lead disclosures.
rationales: Replace arbitrary exclusions with competing report-scope interpretations.
Natural paraphrase of disclosure scope; remove keyed common-area echo.
Retain relevance limitation for multiunit lead records.

before: A contractor removes visible mold but leaves an active roof leak. Why is the remediation incomplete?
Every mold spore must be eliminated permanently
Federal clearance requires a fixed spore count
Repainting is required before repairing the leak
EPA identifies correcting the water problem as essential to preventing recurrence. It does not establish a federal indoor mold-count clearance limit.
after: After clean-water damage, which EPA-recommended drying window helps prevent mold growth in building materials?

EPA recommends drying water-damaged areas and items within 24–48 hours to prevent mold growth. The water source must also be corrected; the drying interval is prevention guidance, not a federal clearance standard.
rationales: Replace obvious leak-restatement with a useful primary-source prevention interval.

before: Environmental records omit a former industrial use. How should a significant gap affecting conclusions be handled in AAI?
Identify its effect on the professional’s assessment
Treat the missing period as presumed uncontaminated
Substitute present zoning for the missing use history
Use a clean title report to resolve the environmental gap
EPA requires identification of significant data gaps affecting the environmental professional’s ability to assess releases or threatened releases.
after: AAI cannot reconstruct decades of industrial occupancy. Which report finding addresses that limitation?
Significant data gap affecting the professional’s opinion
Confirmed release requiring a quantified cleanup estimate
Recorded land-use restriction limiting future development

Missing historical information can limit the professional’s ability to assess releases. The report must identify significant gaps and their effects; absence of records alone does not establish a confirmed release, a recorded restriction, or completed cleanup.
rationales: Use credible report findings rather than absurd substitutes.

before: A buyer completes AAI before closing. What prevents that step alone from guaranteeing continuing CERCLA protection?
Federal approval of every deed conveying the property
Automatic termination of protection when occupancy begins
Unanimous consent from every former site operator
EPA explains that liability protections require meeting other criteria and continuing obligations after acquisition; AAI is one part of the process.
after: Which action is a continuing CERCLA landowner obligation rather than part of the pre-acquisition AAI investigation?

EPA distinguishes investigation before acquisition from continuing obligations afterward. Complying with land-use restrictions and preserving institutional controls are continuing duties; the other choices are components of investigating the site before acquisition.
rationales: Replace blanket no-immunity truism with before/after obligation distinction.

before: A home in a Special Flood Hazard Area has a government-backed mortgage. Which insurance issue follows?
Flood coverage is required for the loan
A standard homeowners policy satisfies the requirement
A buyer’s acknowledgment replaces required coverage
Coverage waits until a presidential disaster declaration
NFIP guidance identifies the special-hazard-area and government-backed-mortgage combination as triggering required flood coverage.
after: A home in a Special Flood Hazard Area secures a government-backed mortgage. Which coverage addresses the mandatory flood requirement?

NFIP guidance requires flood coverage for this hazard-area and financing combination. Homeowners insurance, mortgage default insurance and a home warranty cover different risks and do not satisfy the flood requirement.
rationales: Use competing insurance categories rather than unreasonable substitutes.

before: Why should a commercial buyer investigate a leaking underground fuel tank beyond the tank’s physical repair cost?
Contamination may extend beyond the tank excavation
Liability is limited to repairing the leaking equipment
Tank replacement includes verified groundwater cleanup
Disconnected tanks cannot present residual release risks
EPA identifies contamination of soil and groundwater as a principal UST hazard. Repairing the equipment does not by itself resolve a prior release.
after: A removed fuel tank left petroleum in surrounding soil. Which pathway could carry contamination into nearby drinking-water wells?

EPA identifies seepage through soil into groundwater as a major UST release hazard. Removing the tank stops neither existing subsurface contamination nor its potential migration toward groundwater supplies.
rationales: Replace caution-versus-assurances choices with competing exposure pathways.

before: A heating-oil tank serves only the building where it is located. What follows from its federal UST exclusion?
State or local tank rules may still apply
Federal exclusion preempts state tank regulation
Exclusion depends on obtaining a federal closure permit
The tank becomes subject to federal petroleum rules instead
EPA lists on-premises heating-oil tanks among federal UST exclusions while warning that state or local requirements may still apply.
EPA-UST:Do all tanks meet federal regulations
after: Federal UST classification uses a ten-percent burial threshold. Which capacity is used to calculate that percentage?
Tank and connected underground piping combined
Tank shell capacity excluding connected piping
Petroleum currently stored in the tank
Daily fuel throughput of the system

EPA defines an underground storage tank system using at least ten percent of its combined tank-and-connected-piping volume underground. This is a capacity-based definition, not a test of current fill or daily throughput; separate exclusions and state rules can still matter.
rationales: Replace generic state-may-regulate answer with precise system-definition distinction.
Ask denominator without key-only underground/piping echoes.

before: A qualified applicant relies on pension income. Which underwriting distinction is consistent with ECOA guidance?
Assess amount and continuity without categorical exclusion
Exclude the income because employment has ended
Count pension income only for applicants below retirement age
Replace income verification with the applicant’s age
CFPB says lenders may consider amount and likely continuation of income but may not reject it simply because of its protected source.
after: Equal monthly pensions have different documented expiration dates. Which distinction may a lender evaluate under ECOA?
Current monthly amount of qualifying income

CFPB permits considering income amount and likely continuation. These pensions have equal current payments and the same source category, but their documented duration differs; no difference in existing debts is given.
rationales: Narrow ECOA to factual continuity assessment with competing underwriting inputs.
Replace overtly discriminatory strawmen with competing financial attributes; stem supplies distinguishing facts.
Match explanation to revised financial-attribute distractors.

before: Zoning permits an office, but a valid covenant prohibits it. What must a broker evaluate?
DRE Title distinguishes public zoning from private restrictions. Permission under one does not establish compliance with the other.
after: Zoning permits an office, but a valid covenant prohibits it. What must a broker evaluate?
DRE Title distinguishes public zoning from private restrictions. Permission under one does not establish compliance with the other.
rationales: Cognitive label only: single-rule application or stipulated calculation, not demonstrated analysis.

before: An access grant benefits Parcel A. Its owner buys Parcel B next door. What determines use for Parcel B?
DRE Title defines an easement by its specified purpose and benefited property. Acquiring another parcel does not itself establish that the existing grant serves it.
after: An access grant benefits Parcel A. Its owner buys Parcel B next door. What determines use for Parcel B?
DRE Title defines an easement by its specified purpose and benefited property. Acquiring another parcel does not itself establish that the existing grant serves it.
rationales: Cognitive label only: single-rule application or stipulated calculation, not demonstrated analysis.

before: A 40% cotenant fences off the front 40% for exclusive use. What additional basis would justify that allocation?
A deed confirming the fractional interest
A record of the original purchase price
An appraisal allocating 40% of its value
DRE Title explains that tenancy in common gives undivided interests and common possession. A fractional ownership interest alone does not assign an exclusive physical area.
after: A 40% cotenant fences off the front 40% for exclusive use. What additional basis would justify that allocation?
A deed confirming the fractional interest
A record of the original purchase price
An appraisal allocating 40% of its value
DRE Title explains that tenancy in common gives undivided interests and common possession. A fractional ownership interest alone does not assign an exclusive physical area.
rationales: Cognitive label only: single-rule application or stipulated calculation, not demonstrated analysis.

before: Alex and Bea hold title with survivorship. Alex's will leaves everything to Lee. Who receives Alex's interest?
Bea and Lee, as tenants in common
DRE Title identifies survivorship as controlling an intact joint tenancy interest. A will does not redirect that interest into probate.
after: Alex and Bea hold title with survivorship. Alex's will leaves everything to Lee. Who receives Alex's interest?
Bea and Lee, as tenants in common
DRE Title identifies survivorship as controlling an intact joint tenancy interest. A will does not redirect that interest into probate.
rationales: Cognitive label only: single-rule application or stipulated calculation, not demonstrated analysis.

before: An occupant claims an unrecorded purchase option; the seller denies it. Which evidence resolves the conflict most directly?
Seller's recorded deed and acquisition date
